$comment: The extended shape of the `foundry` manifest block every role package may declare in its own package.json. `assessment` already exists (docs/DECISIONS.md and packages/controller/src/onboarding/discovery.ts); version 1 of this contract ADDED `intake`, `outputs`, `status`, and `fit` beside it. Version 2 (owner decision on #1176, 2026-09-22, recorded in that issue's and #1172's comments) adds `solves`, `needs`, and `feeds`, so Advisor can compose a kit per client from package self-descriptions instead of a fixed grouping. Nothing here is inferred: @clossys/controller's onboarding discovery reads each field only from the installed package's own manifest, never from a generic template, and an absent field is reported as absent -- never guessed, never defaulted. scripts/check-package-framework.mjs is the gate that validates any of these fields a package DOES declare; it does not require any of them yet (see `enforcement`). Version 3 (issue #1196, owner decision 2026-09-22) adds `capabilities`: a MECE definition of each role's craft, checked within a role (its own sub-questions jointly answer its job question, no two capabilities produce the same output) and across roles (every capability and every output has exactly one owner, every `needs` is fed by exactly one capability). This wave builds the schema and the gate only -- the per-role maps (#1198-#1202) for the five v0 Launch-pack roles land directly in this repository, owner option A (2026-09-22, issue #1187), checked across roles by the gate and held under the `owner-review` label until the owner clears it; the remaining roles' own maps still land later, so `--enforce` runs against an allowlisted set until they do.

assessment.meaning: The role's first-day assessment entry point: a bin this same manifest maps, invoked with one caller-owned JSON evidence file and a 0/1/2 (satisfied/violated/indeterminate) exit.

intake.shape: a package-relative path string to one shipped JSON file
intake.meaning: What the role must know before it walks, as a set of stable, multiple-choice question cards -- the shape @clossys/advisor already uses for sponsor questions (SponsorQuestionCard, packages/advisor/src/sponsor-questions.ts). The referenced file's own shape is docs/contracts/intake-question-cards.json.
intake.pathRule: relative, must resolve inside the package directory (no leading '/', no '..' segment)

outputs.shape: a non-empty array of package-relative path strings
outputs.meaning: The files this role owns and may write, declared so Advisor, Launcher, and every skill can list what a role produces without reading its source. Every path must fall under this role's own `clossys/<role>/` folder, per the layout docs/contracts/consumer-layout.json defines (issue #1171). `<role>` is the manifest's own package name with its scope removed (`@clossys/advisor` -> `clossys/advisor/`).
outputs.pathRule: relative, no leading '/', no '..' segment, first two path segments must be exactly `clossys/<role-name>`

status.meaning: A read-only command that reports where this role currently stands in the consumer's repository -- the baseline every skill opens with before proposing anything. Same invocation contract as `assessment`, but the probe MUST NOT mutate anything it reads.
status.pathRule: the named bin must be one this same manifest's `bin` field maps, exactly like `assessment`

fit.shape: a package-relative path string to one shipped JSON file
fit.meaning: The evidence that makes this role applicable to a repository at all (for example, Publisher needs an audience-facing surface). Advisor reads these to recommend a role instead of guessing. The referenced file's own shape is docs/contracts/fit-signal-declarations.json.
fit.pathRule: relative, must resolve inside the package directory (no leading '/', no '..' segment)

solves.status: new (schema version 2, issue #1172's "De-risking additions to `solves`" comment)
solves.shape: an array of { problem: string, statement: string, metric: string, proofCase: string, evidence: "designed" | "qualified" | "proven" } (may be empty)
solves.meaning: Verifiable claims about which client problems this role solves. Advisor composes a kit per client by matching client-confirmed problems to these entries (issue #1176's "kits are composed, not a fixed grouping" owner decision) instead of a hand-maintained grouping; a composed kit's per-role "why" cites one entry.

entryFields.problem: a stable id from docs/contracts/client-problems.json (owned by the Advisor lane, issue #1176). That file does not exist in every wave -- see `problemIdRule`.
entryFields.statement: one sentence, role-specific wording in the client's own words: one problem per entry, no solution language, no jargon
entryFields.metric: must equal this role's OWN owned metric name in docs/contracts/role-loop-archetypes.json (`roles[<role>].metric.name`) -- a claim that cannot be measured cannot be made
entryFields.proofCase: a case id from this role's own qualification adapter, governance/release-qualification-adapters/<role>/current-direct.json (`cases[].id`), showing the role's own check actually detects the problem
entryFields.evidence: `designed` (claimed, untested), `qualified` (a proof case passes in a retained qualification record), or `proven` (independent outcome evidence from a real engagement -- issue #1189's feedback loop)
entryFields.capability: optional: the id of one of this role's own `capabilities[].id` entries that backs this claim -- how a solves entry maps a client problem onto the capability that actually solves it (issue #1196). Omitted when this role has not yet declared `capabilities`.

solves.problemIdRule: lowercase kebab-case (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`). When docs/contracts/client-problems.json does not exist yet, a `problem` id is validated by this format rule only; once that file exists, its declared ids become the resolved vocabulary and an id it does not declare is a finding under `--enforce`.

needs.shape: an array of { producerRole: string, artifact: string } (may be empty)
needs.meaning: Artifacts this role consumes from another role's own output (for example, Designer needs Strategist's `direction`). Advisor uses these to pull in upstream roles and order the collaboration when composing a kit.
needs.enforcedRule: under --enforce, every `needs` entry must match some role's `feeds` entry naming the same `artifact`, sourced from `producerRole`'s own manifest -- and the resulting role -> producerRole handoff graph across every active role must have no cycle.

feeds.shape: an array of { artifact: string, path: string } (may be empty)
feeds.meaning: Artifacts this role produces for other roles to consume.
feeds.pathRule: same rule as `outputs`: relative, no leading '/', no '..' segment, first two path segments must be exactly `clossys/<role-name>`

capabilities.shape: a non-empty array of { id, subQuestion, worldClass, inputs, outputs, proofCase, maturity, v0, businessLifecycleStage } (may be omitted entirely; a role that declares it must declare at least one entry)
capabilities.meaning: A MECE (mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive) definition of what a world-class practitioner of this role does. Together across every active role, the maps leave no capability ownerless and no capability owned twice -- the catalogue view issue #1196 asks for lays every declared capability along the business lifecycle so gaps and overlaps are visible.

entryFields.id: stable, kebab-case, unique within this role's own capabilities array
entryFields.subQuestion: one sub-question of this role's own job question (docs/contracts/role-loop-archetypes.json, roles[<role>].jobQuestion). Every capability's subQuestion together must jointly answer that job question -- a judgment call this gate reports on (whether every declared capability's subQuestion is distinct, and flags when zero capabilities are declared) but does not claim to verify semantically; the completeness judgment itself belongs to the role package and its reviewer, not to a mechanical check.
entryFields.worldClass: one sentence: the standard this capability is held to
entryFields.inputs: an array of { producerRole, artifact } -- client intake plus `needs` from other roles this capability actually consumes; same shape as the top-level `needs` field
entryFields.outputs: a non-empty array of package-relative paths, same `pathRule` as the top-level `outputs` field -- the files this ONE capability owns. No two capabilities across this role's own array may declare the same output path, and (under --enforce) no two capabilities across every active role may either: every output has exactly one owner.
entryFields.proofCase: a case id from this role's own qualification adapter (governance/release-qualification-adapters/<role>/current-direct.json, cases[].id) showing this capability actually works, or `null` when `maturity` is `planned`. scripts/check-capability-maps.mjs checks this pairing structurally (`planned` iff `null`) and, when this role's own adapter file exists, resolves a non-null `proofCase` against that file's own `cases[].id` -- a capability sharing another capability's or another gate's case is a finding unless the fixture genuinely exercises both. INTERIM (tracked by issue #1272, opened when the five v0 Launch-pack maps first landed): each role's retained adapter currently has only ONE case, so most `built`/`partial` capabilities in those five maps cite that one anchor case rather than a case that genuinely exercises them -- an acknowledged, disclosed gap (stated in each affected package's own CHANGELOG entry), not a claim that the anchor proves them. #1272 lists every such pair and tracks adding a dedicated, verified case for each one; the rule going forward is: add a real case, or drop the capability to `partial`.
entryFields.maturity: `built` (working today), `partial` (partially working), or `planned` (roadmap only) -- derived from evidence, not declared aspiration. `planned` is the honest answer to "can it do X today?". Joint with `proofCase`: `planned` REQUIRES `proofCase: null` (nothing proves a capability that doesn't exist yet); `built`/`partial` REQUIRE a real, nonempty `proofCase`.
entryFields.v0: boolean: whether this capability is part of the first deliverable a new product owes (the v0 Launch pack, issue #1187's plan)
entryFields.businessLifecycleStage: optional: one of `found`, `define`, `build`, `launch`, `acquire`, `convert`, `deliver`, `operate`, `learn` -- where this capability sits on the client's own business lifecycle, the axis the catalogue view lays every role's capabilities along.

capabilities.enforcedRule: within one role (both report mode and --enforce): no two capabilities share an output path, at least one capability is declared (a role declaring an empty `capabilities` array has nothing to check and is a malformed declaration, not an absence), and every capability's own `inputs` entry resolves -- `{ producerRole, artifact }` must name a capability whose own `id` is `artifact`, declared among `producerRole`'s own well-formed capabilities (forgiven when `producerRole` is itself allowlisted, since its map hasn't landed yet). This last check runs in BOTH modes, not only --enforce, because it only needs the one named producer role's own manifest, unlike the two checks below which need every active role's manifest to answer at once. Under --enforce only, ACROSS every active role: no output path is claimed by more than one capability (of any role); and every top-level `needs`/`feeds` entry is fed by exactly one capability's own declared `outputs` entry naming the same artifact -- a SEPARATE mechanism from capability-`inputs` resolution above, since a capability's own `inputs` resolves directly against a producer's capability id, never against a top-level `feeds` path.

enforcement.rule: scripts/check-package-framework.mjs runs in REPORT MODE by default: it prints a conformance table for every package in packages/*, and fails ONLY when a field a package DOES declare is malformed (wrong shape, an unmapped bin, an escaping or misplaced path, or -- for `solves` -- a field missing or an `evidence` value outside the declared enum). Absence of intake, outputs, status, fit, solves, needs, or feeds is never a failure in report mode -- it is printed and counted, the same discipline check-role-assessment-surfaces.mjs already applies to `assessment` (issue #435: a capability requiring zero targets must not grade identically to one fully covered). Pass --enforce to fail on absence too, plus the deeper checks version 2 adds: a `solves.metric` that does not name this role's own owned metric, a `solves.proofCase` that does not exist in this role's own qualification adapter, two roles whose `solves` claim the same `problem` id (a boundary decision, the #504/#505 class), a `problem` id in docs/contracts/client-problems.json that no role claims (only once that file exists), an unmatched `needs` entry, or a cycle in the needs/feeds handoff graph. `--enforce` is for a later wave, once packages have had the chance to conform (issue #1172's own sequencing: the five Launch-kit packages first, then the remaining roles). Version 3 (issue #1196) adds `capabilities` to the same report-mode-by-default, then-enforce discipline: absence is never a failure in report mode, and `--enforce` adds the MECE checks the field's own `enforcedRule` states. scripts/check-capability-maps.mjs is the dedicated gate for this field -- kept separate from scripts/check-package-framework.mjs the way check-role-assessment-surfaces.mjs already is, since the MECE checks (cross-role output ownership, needs/capability-output matching) are their own concern.

governance.rule: No single package owns this framework at runtime. It is supplier governance: this contract plus the gate that reads it. @clossys/controller's onboarding discovers a role's declarations at runtime and never infers one; @clossys/advisor orchestrates what discovery returns. Neither package gains a new runtime dependency on any role package to do this -- discovery reads an installed manifest, nothing else.
governance.changeProcedure: A framework change is exactly one pull request: it bumps this file's own top-level `version`, and brings every package this repository ships into conformance with the new shape in the same change. A package left non-conformant after that PR is a defect, not a follow-up.

lifecycle.$comment: The one lifecycle vocabulary for every capability and pack item (issue #1228), exported in code as packages/controller/src/loop/lifecycle.ts. Not itself a `fields` entry -- no manifest key declares it -- because it is the shared state model the loop engine (docs/contracts/loop.json, issue #1195) and pack items (issue #1204) each specialize, not a per-role declaration.

loop.$comment: The loop engine (issue #1195): one sense -> judge -> act -> verify -> learn loop every role runs, implemented once in @clossys/controller (packages/controller/src/loop/*). Not a fields entry -- no manifest key declares it -- because every active role runs the same engine; there is nothing role-specific to declare here beyond the outputs/feeds this contract already covers.
